surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the exchange of B–H and O–H surface species during the ALD process. The Hf(BH4)4 precursor reacts with surface hydroxyls to form an adsorbed Hf(BH4)x complex. Subsequent H2O exposure leads to the removal of B–H groups and the creation of O–H groups, resulting in the formation of borate segments and the accumulation of boron oxide in the as-grown films.
evidence: In situ FTIR measurements showed that the surface chemistry proceeds by the exchange of B–H and O–H surface species. After the Hf(BH4)4 exposure, positive absorbance features at 2575 cm−1 and 2126 cm−1 (attributed to B–H stretching) and a negative peak at 3695 cm−1 (attributed to O–H stretch) were observed. Following H2O exposure, the B–H groups were removed, and O–H groups were created, indicating the formation of borate segments and the accumulation of boron oxide in the as-grown films.
